378 The Last Oil Baron: Leon Hess

Episode 378 · February 10, 2025 · 53m
Listen: Audio

Notes

Your father goes bankrupt. You work for 50 cents a day to try to help your family survive the Great Depression. At 19 you see an opportunity where others see nothing. You start “a little fuel delivery business” with one used truck. Five years later you have 10 trucks. World War II breaks out and you serve as the fuel supply officer for General Patton.

...

You take your company public. You merge with an oil exploration firm. You build the largest refinery in the Western Hemisphere. You buy the New York Jets. You built your “little fuel delivery business” into a multibillion-dollar, multinational, vertically integrated energy behemoth. You are Leon Hess, founder of the Hess family dynasty.
This episode is what I learned from reading Hess: The Last Oil Baron by Tina Davis and Jessica Resnick-Ault.

(Reuters) By Jessica Resnick-Ault – Alternative investment management group Oaktree Capital Management L.P. has purchased Hess Corp’s  share of proprietary energy trader HETCO, and will inject $500 million to fund the New York-based outfit’s expansion into new commodity markets.
The deal, the latest shareholder shake-up in the commodities trading industry, comes more than a year and a half after Hess launched the sale of Hess Energy Trading (HETCO), a small firm run by two former Goldman Sachs partners that trades physical oil, natural gas and other energy markets. Investors urged Hess Corp to divest the unit, saying it weighed on its balance sheet.
The main founders of HETCO, Stephen Hendel and Stephen Semlitz, will remain with the company after the acquisition, they said in a statement. No financial details were released.

...

Earlier this year, the company sold its network of East Coast gasoline stations and terminals that were not seen as key to its core mission of exploring and producing oil.
HETCO, one of the last pieces to be sold, was established in 1997, and has grown to become a regular, if niche, player in many of the world’s benchmark energy markets.

...

Net realized gains on trading activities amounted to $191 million in 2013 and $60 million in 2012, according to Hess Corp’s annual filing.
